subproblem.title: Slicing of integer multiplicity currents by a Lipschitz function (Simon Ch. 6, 4.1–4.5)
subproblem.statement:
Assume (C1), the frozen statement of the sibling-of-parent node dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity triple R in U representing T, M_W(T) = μ_R(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple RT = (M, θ, ξ), and ∂T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by an integer multiplicity triple RB = (M', θ', ξ'). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz. Then there are currents P_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U), t ∈ ℝ, such that:
(1) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt ≤ L·M_W(T);
(2) for L¹-a.e. t: P_t is integer multiplicity; P_t(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose support is disjoint from f⁻¹(t); and P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dH^{n+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
Remark (no additional claim): the identity in (2) says P_t = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} on 𝒟ⁿ(U), which is Simon's formula 4.5(2) for the slice ⟨T, f, t⟩ (Ch. 6, 4.4–4.5).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) ∧ T.support = U ∩ R.measure.support) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (RT : IMRep U (n + 1)) (RB : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), IsOpen U → RT.Represents T → RB.Represents T.boundary → LipschitzWith L f → ∃ Ps : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → AEMeasurable (fun t => (Ps t).massOn W) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (Ps t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * T.massOn W) ∧ ∀ᵐ t, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ps t) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) (f ⁻¹' {t}) → Ps t ω = 0) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Ps t ω = (∫ x in RT.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RT.mult x : ℝ) * RT.orient x (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n + 1]) - ∫ x in RB.carrier ∩ {x | f x < t}, (RB.mult x : ℝ) * RB.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §4: Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4 and Lemma 4.5(1),(2) with their printed proofs (chapter-06.txt lines 1156–1310). These are applied to the (n+1)-current T, so slices are n-currents. The proof also uses Ch. 3, 2.1 (tangential gradient) and 2.7–2.10 (co-area formula, slices of rectifiable sets) (chapter-03.txt lines 327–440), and the hypothesis (C1) for mass identities.
Notation: M, θ, ξ are the fields of RT and M', θ', ξ' those of RB; Hᵐ = μHE[m]. ∇^M f is the tangential gradient of f on M (Ch. 3, 2.1). It is defined H^{n+1}-a.e. on M via the decomposition M = ⋃_j M_j with M_j ⊆ N_j, N_j embedded C¹ (n+1)-submanifolds (Ch. 3, Remark 1.3), and T_xM = T_xN_j a.e. on M_j (Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2); compare sibling tangent_locality). It satisfies ∇^M f(x) ∈ T_xM and |∇^M f| ≤ L. Fix Borel versions. M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^M f(x) ≠ 0} and M_t := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t).
1. (Lemma 4.1.) For L¹-a.e. t:
 (a) M_t is countably n-rectifiable (Ch. 3, 2.10(2)).
 (b) For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t, T_xM_t and T_xM exist and T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f(x) orthogonally (Ch. 3, 1.6 and 2.1, applied on the C¹ pieces N_j).
 (c) Co-area formula (Ch. 3, 2.9 with m = 1, where J^M_f* = |∇^M f|): for every non-negative H^{n+1}-measurable g on M, t ↦ ∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ is L¹-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g dHⁿ dt = ∫_M |∇^M f| g dH^{n+1}.
2. (4.3–4.4: the slices.) Fix an exhaustion of U by compact sets K_i. Let Z_bad ⊆ M be the H^{n+1}-null set of points where T_xM does not exist, or ξ(x) does not orient T_xM, or the chosen Borel versions of ξ and ∇^M f differ from the true ones. Let G₁ be the set of t for which 1(a), 1(b) hold, ∫_{M_t∩K_i}θ dHⁿ < ∞ for all i, and Hⁿ(Z_bad ∩ M_t) = 0. G₁ has full measure: use 1(c) with g = θ1_{K_i} (note ∫_{M∩K_i}|∇^M f|θ ≤ L∫_{M∩K_i}θ < ∞), and 1(c) with g = 1_{Z_bad}, which gives ∫ Hⁿ(Z_bad ∩ M_t) dt = ∫_{Z_bad}|∇^M f| dH^{n+1} = 0.
 (a) For t ∈ G₁ and x ∈ M_t ∖ Z_bad (so for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_t) put ν(x) := ∇^M f(x)/|∇^M f(x)| and ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ⌞ ν(x), i.e. ξ_t(x)(α) := ξ(x)(ν(x)♭ ∧ α) for n-covectors α; there ξ(x) orients T_xM.
 (b) If τ₁,…,τₙ is an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t, then (ν, τ₁,…,τₙ) is an orthonormal basis of T_xM by 1(b). So ξ(x) = ±ν∧τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ and ξ_t(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ orients T_xM_t.
 (c) Hence R_t := (M_t, θ|M_t, ξ_t) is an integer multiplicity triple in U: M_t ⊆ M ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, θ ≥ 1 on M_t, θ is locally integrable on M_t since t ∈ G₁, and ξ_t is measurable.
 (d) Apply the sibling borel_restriction to R_t and A := ℝ^P. It gives P_t ∈ 𝒟_n(U) represented by the triple with carrier M_t ∩ ℝ^P = M_t, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ_t, i.e. by R_t. Thus P_t(ω) = ∫_{M_t} θ ξ_t(ω) dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). For t ∉ G₁ put P_t := 0.
3. Support property. For t ∈ G₁, M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t). If spt ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅ then ω = 0 on M_t, so P_t(ω) = 0.
4. (4.5(1): mass.) Let W be open.
 (a) For t ∈ G₁, (C1) applied to P_t and R_t gives M_W(P_t) = μ_{R_t}(W) = ∫_{M_t∩W}θ dHⁿ.
 (b) By 1(c) with g = θ1_W, t ↦ ∫_{M_t∩W}θ dHⁿ is measurable. So t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable.
 (c) ∫ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ dH^{n+1} ≤ L ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^{n+1} = L·μ_{RT}(W) = L·M_W(T). The last equality is (C1) for T.
5. (4.5(2): slice identity, following Simon's printed proof.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0.
 (a) Cut-off. Let γ : ℝ → [0,1] be 1 on (−∞, t − ε], 0 on [t, ∞) and linear in between. Let h := γ∘f (Lipschitz) and let h_δ be its mollifications: C^∞, h_δ → h locally uniformly, |∇h_δ| ≤ Lip h.
 (b) Since h_δω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and d(h_δω) = dh_δ ∧ ω + h_δ dω,
 (i) ∂T(h_δω) = T(dh_δ ∧ ω) + T(h_δ dω).
 (c) Limits δ → 0 of the outer terms: ∂T(h_δω) = ∫_{M'} θ' h_δ ξ'(ω) → ∫_{M'} θ' h ξ'(ω), and T(h_δ dω) → ∫_M θ h ξ(dω), by dominated convergence.
 (d) Middle term. Since ξ(x) orients T_xM, ξ(x)(dh_δ ∧ ω) depends only on the tangential part ∇^M h_δ = P_{T_xM}∇h_δ. By Simon's step (1), v·∇^M h_δ → v·∇^M h weakly in L²(μ_T) for bounded measurable v; this is checked on the C¹ pieces N_j. By the chain rule (Ch. 3, 2.1), ∇^M h = γ'(f)∇^M f H^{n+1}-a.e. on M, using also ∇^M f = 0 a.e. on each level set {f = c}.
 (e) Letting δ → 0 in (i) gives
 (ii) ∫_{M'} θ' h ξ'(ω) dHⁿ = −ε⁻¹ ∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θ |∇^M f| ξ(ν♭ ∧ ω) dH^{n+1} + ∫_M θ h ξ(dω) dH^{n+1};
 the integrand of the middle term vanishes on M ∖ M₊.
 (f) Co-area. Apply 1(c) to the positive and negative parts of θ ξ(ν♭∧ω) 1_{t−ε<f<t}, and use ∫_{M_s} θ ξ(ν♭∧ω) dHⁿ = P_s(ω) for s ∈ G₁. The middle term of (ii) equals −ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^t P_s(ω) ds, and s ↦ P_s(ω) is in L¹_loc by 1(c) (Remark 4.2).
 (g) Let ε ↓ 0. Then h ↑ 1_{f<t} pointwise, so the left side of (ii) tends to ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'ξ'(ω) and the last term to ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θξ(dω), by dominated convergence. Also ε⁻¹∫_{t−ε}^t P_s(ω) ds → P_t(ω) at every Lebesgue point t of s ↦ P_s(ω). Hence, for a.e. t,
 (iii) P_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ ξ(dω) dH^{n+1} − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ' ξ'(ω) dHⁿ.
6. Independence of ω.
 (a) Choose a countable family {ω_i} ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) such that every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is the limit of a sequence ω_{i_k} with supports in a common compact K ⊆ U and ω_{i_k} → ω, dω_{i_k} → dω uniformly. Such a family exists by separability of C¹_c on each compact piece of an exhaustion.
 (b) Let G₂ ⊆ G₁ be the full-measure set of t for which (iii) holds for all ω_i.
 (c) For t ∈ G₂, each term of (iii) is an integral of ω or dω against a measure that is finite on K (θξ_tHⁿ⌞M_t, θξH^{n+1}⌞M, θ'ξ'Hⁿ⌞M'). So each term is continuous under this convergence, and (iii) holds for every ω. Simon: "by considering a countable dense set of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) … except for a set F of t having L¹-measure zero, with F independent of ω".
7. Conclusion. The family (P_t) satisfies (1) by step 4. For every t ∈ G₂, a full-measure set: P_t is integer multiplicity (step 2), P_t vanishes on forms whose support misses f⁻¹(t) (step 3), and P_t satisfies (iii) for every ω, which is the stated identity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 4.1: for a.e. t, M_t = f⁻¹(t) ∩ {∇^M f ≠ 0} is countably n-rectifiable with T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f; co-area formula on M.
For a.e. t, R_t = (M_t, θ, ξ⌞ν) is an integer multiplicity triple carried by f⁻¹(t); borel_restriction (with A = ℝ^P) gives the current P_t it represents; P_t := 0 otherwise.
(C1) and co-area give ∫ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_{M∩W}|∇^M f|θ ≤ L·M_W(T).
Simon's mollified cut-off argument gives P_t = ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} at Lebesgue points; a countable dense family of forms makes the null set independent of ω.

audit.reason: The cited rectifiable slicing and coarea results provide the slice carriers and mass estimate. The supplied orientation construction, mollified cutoff argument, and countable dense family establish the identity outside one null set independent of the test form.
